title: Dollarback Alternatives (2026): 6 Shopify Cashback Apps Compared
summary: Compare 6 Dollarback alternatives for Shopify, from store credit and points cashback to event-triggered cashback paid in real money.

## Introduction


Dollarback alternatives are worth comparing on one question before any other. What kind of cashback does the shopper actually get?


Dollarback is one of several cashback and gamification apps Shopify brands find on the Shopify App Store. Lining them up by feature list misses the bigger split.


Some cashback comes back as store credit to spend with you again. Some comes back as real money, paid out when a real world event happens.


This is Playably's own blog.[Playably](https://playably.ai/) runs the event-triggered kind, so we lay out all six types, say where each fits, and keep rival prices and payout rates out of it.


Each app lists its own plan on its Shopify App Store listing.


### Key Takeaways


- Dollarback alternatives split into store credit cashback and event-triggered cashback.
- Store credit cashback is funded by your store when the shopper redeems.
- Playably pays shoppers 100% of their order back by Venmo or PayPal.
- With Playably, the brand pays $0 of the rebate and keeps full margin.


## Two Kinds of Cashback


Store credit cashback rewards a purchase with a balance the shopper spends back in your store. The reward comes with the purchase, as a share of the order.


Event-triggered cashback ties the reward to something outside the store. If the published trigger hits, the shopper gets money back.


If it doesn't, they keep what they bought at the price they paid.


Those two models solve different problems. Store credit chases the second order.


Event-triggered cashback gives shoppers a reason to buy now, at full price, with a headline-sized promise.


How the cost lands is the other difference, and it is where margin goes. For the math on a single order, see[cash back vs discount codes](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/cash-back-vs-discount-codes) .

## 1. Percentage-Back Store Credit Apps


These apps return a set share of each order as store credit.


They give a shopper a clear reason to come back. The reward is small and certain, which suits a high-frequency product.


The cost sits with you. Each redeemed credit is product given away on a later order.


**Good fit:** brands with fast repeat cycles that want a steady return-visit habit. If your list already waits for deals, read[how discount fatigue sets in](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/discount-fatigue) first.


## 2. Next-Order Discount Cashback


Some apps frame cashback as a discount on the shopper's next purchase rather than a stored balance.


It works the same way in practice. The shopper pays full price today and less tomorrow.


That keeps today's price clean and moves the cost to the second order. It also means the reward only matters if the shopper comes back.


**Good fit:** brands focused on bringing lapsed buyers back. For other ways to do that, see[win back customers without discounts](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/win-back-customers-without-discounts) .


## 3. Loyalty Points With a Cashback Option


Loyalty apps reward purchases with points, and some let shoppers redeem them as cashback-style credit.


Points build over time. That suits a loyal base that buys often, and gives a regular shopper a reason to stay.


The payout is deferred, not removed. When points convert, your store still funds the reward.


**Good fit:** brands with a long repeat cycle. For the wider playbook, see[gamification for loyalty programs](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/gamification-strategies-for-loyalty-programs-keeping-customers-coming-back) .


## 4. Gift Card Cashback


Gift card cashback pays the shopper back with a gift card instead of credit or money.


Depending on the app, the card may be for your store or for another retailer. Who funds it, and when, varies by app.


Read the terms closely. Ask who pays the card's value, and what happens to a card the shopper never redeems.


**Good fit:** brands that want a reward with a gift feel. If you'd rather compare it against cash in hand, the team can walk you through both when you[book a Playably demo](https://playably.ai/pages/book-a-demo) .


## 5. Gamified Reward Apps


Gamified apps put a short game in front of the shopper and unlock a reward at the end, usually a discount or a perk.


The game earns attention and an email. The reward still comes from your store when it is a discount.


Playably offers one of these too.[The PlayAbly app](https://apps.shopify.com/playably) is listed on the Shopify App Store as free, with swipe-to-shop and product matchup formats, email capture and a real time dashboard, and needs no coding.


**Good fit:** brands that want engagement and list growth first. More in[gamified email capture](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/gamified-email-capture) .


## 6. Event-Triggered Cashback (Playably)


Playably runs a gamified conditional rebate tied to a real world trigger event.


Shoppers buy at full price and get auto-entered, with no code to remember. If the trigger hits, Playably pays them 100% of their order back, directly, by Venmo or PayPal, usually within days.


Playably insures and hedges the payout, so the brand pays $0 of the rebate and keeps its full margin. Playably carries the payout, so your store never books the liability.


It also reaches the repeat purchase that store credit chases. Soul CBD's OVERTIME Big Game Cashback reached "1.4× the subscription sign-up rate: 59% of campaign buyers subscribed, compared with 41% of other shoppers that same week."


Those subscribers stayed. "63% renewed at least once, close to Soul's regular subscribers (67%)."


Baskets were "16% bigger than the rest of the store ($99 vs. $86)." The mechanic itself is laid out in[how gamified rebates work](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/gamified-rebates-the-full-price-promotion-that-pays-shoppers-back-when-a-real-world-event-hits) .


**Good fit:** Shopify brands that want a full-price offer with a headline promise, without funding the payout.


## What Each Option Costs Your Margin


Plan fees are the easy part to compare. Each app lists its own plan on the Shopify App Store.


The bigger cost is the payout. With options 1 to 4, and with a discount reward in option 5, your store funds the reward when it is redeemed.


With Playably, the brand pays $0 of the rebate. Playably prices campaigns on performance, so you only pay when a sale happens, and Playably carries all the risk.


Two builds sit beside the campaign.[The Tier 1 build fee](https://playably.ai/products/tier-1-build-fee) is about $1,500 one time for a gamified email and landing page test with a quiz and a dedicated brand strategist, plus a 15% revenue share on transactions from shoppers who played the game or gave their email during play.


[The bespoke shoppable game build](https://playably.ai/products/build-fee-bespoke-shoppable-game-build) is estimated at $10K to $25K, based on the complexity of the game concept, custom illustrations and development requirements.


## Which Cashback Type Fits Your Store


Match the type to the job.


- **Steady repeat visits from a loyal base?** Store credit or points.
- **Lapsed buyers?** Next-order cashback.
- **A gift feel?** Gift card cashback, after reading the terms.
- **Attention and email capture?** A gamified reward app.
- **Full-price conversion around a moment, with the payout off your books?** Event-triggered cashback.


Brands can run more than one. A gamified app can grow the list while an event-triggered rebate runs the headline offer.


Whatever the mix, keep the data. In a Playably campaign, each play returns zero party data that feeds segmentation, recommendations and lifecycle flows.


Who else runs rebate promotions, and how they pay out, is covered in[conditional rebate promotions in 2026](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/conditional-rebate-promotions-for-ecommerce-in-2026-who-runs-them-who-pays-out-and-what-they-cost) .


## Conclusion


Dollarback alternatives come down to which cashback you want your shoppers to get. Store credit, a next-order discount, points, a gift card, a game reward, or real money tied to a real event.


The first five keep the payout with your store or the app's terms. Playably's event-triggered cashback pays shoppers 100% of their order back when the trigger hits, and the brand pays $0 of the rebate.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the main Dollarback alternatives for Shopify brands?


The main Dollarback alternatives for Shopify brands are percentage-back store credit apps, next-order discount cashback, loyalty points with a cashback option, gift card cashback, gamified reward apps, and event-triggered cashback from Playably. They differ on how shoppers are paid and who funds the payout. With Playably, shoppers buy at full price and the brand pays $0 of the rebate.


### How is store credit cashback different from Playably's event-triggered cashback?


Store credit cashback gives the shopper a balance to spend in your store, and your store funds it when it is redeemed. Playably's event-triggered cashback pays shoppers 100% of their order back by Venmo or PayPal if a real, published trigger hits. Playably insures and hedges that payout, so the store never books the liability.


### Is cashback from a Dollarback alternative like Playably paid in cash or store credit?


Playably pays cashback to the shopper as money through Venmo or PayPal, usually within days, not as store credit or a gift card. Playably pays it directly, which is why the brand pays $0 of the rebate and keeps full margin. When the trigger hits, shoppers get 100% of their order back rather than a voucher to spend again.


### How much does Playably cost compared with other Dollarback alternatives?


Playably prices rebate campaigns on performance, so the brand only pays when a sale happens and Playably carries all the risk. No rate is published for the campaign itself, and Playably frames the cost as coming from the discount budget. Other cashback apps list their plans on the Shopify App Store, so compare those listings directly.


### Is an event-triggered Dollarback alternative like Playably gambling?


No. It's a conditional rebate tied to a real, published event, with a no-purchase-necessary path. Nobody is betting. Playably handles the legal work and takes on the compliance for each campaign, and the brand's team approves the brief before the campaign runs. The trigger is a public event anyone can verify.
